analysis_md:
# PCG — PG&E Corporation
v5 run, 2026-10-14 (supersedes the 2026-10-13 v4-era analysis). In scope (market cap $29.417B at $13.3592, nasdaq_quote_api — under the $40B cutoff).

All figures below are copied from dcf_numbers.json, financials_history.csv, ttm.py output, or the cited search results — none are recomputed. **Method change vs the v4 run, stated plainly:** the v4 analysis reached Tier B by pinning the base to a hand-built TTM non-GAAP core EPS figure. v5 does not permit that: TTM figures come only from ttm.py (which cannot produce one for PCG — see STALE_FY), and base/override decisions are main-agent calls recorded in judgment.json fields, of which PCG has none. The v5 result below is therefore the engine's numbers tier, with the sector mismatch documented rather than worked around.

## What it is
Oakland-based holding company for Pacific Gas and Electric Company, the regulated electric and gas utility serving Northern and Central California (~16 million people), plus the Diablo Canyon nuclear plant. Earnings are almost entirely regulator-set: a multi-year wildfire-hardening program (undergrounding, covered conductor, monitoring) drives the rate base. Current prints (company Q2 2026 release, via search results): Q2 2026 GAAP EPS $0.33 and non-GAAP core EPS $0.40; H1 2026 core EPS $0.83 vs $0.64 in H1 2025; full-year 2026 core EPS guidance reaffirmed at $1.64–$1.66; a $73B capital investment plan through 2030 structured to require no additional equity financing; at least 9% annual core EPS growth targeted for 2027 through 2030; a 12+ GW data-center project pipeline; over 1,900 miles of undergrounding planned complete by end-2027. The equity story remains inseparable from wildfire liability: California's inverse-condemnation doctrine drove the 2019–2020 Chapter 11, and SB 254 (signed September 19, 2025) is the legislature's latest attempt to stabilize the framework.

## Owner's earnings
**FY2025 (10-K via EDGAR, from financials_history.csv):** revenue $24,935M; net income $2,703M; operating cash flow $8,716M; capex $11,787M (tag: PaymentsToAcquirePropertyPlantAndEquipment); SBC $134M (tag: AllocatedShareBasedCompensationExpense).
- **Conservative owner's earnings FY2025: −$3,205M = −$1.46/share** (OCF − capex − SBC). Capex exceeds operating cash flow by a wide margin — the structural fact of a utility compounding rate base at high-single digits while running a wildfire-undergrounding program, not a one-off year.
- **OE positive 0 of the last 5 fiscal years** on the conservative definition (FY2021–25: −$5,483M / −$5,978M / −$5,058M / −$2,432M / −$3,205M, from financials_history.csv).
- Maintenance version: **not computable from the engine outputs** — PG&E carries no usable D&A annual tag in EDGAR companyfacts (used_tags da = null), so the engine leaves the maintenance OE column blank for every year. Per the sweep's hard rule this is stated in words rather than filled in by hand.
- **Base used = the engine's normalized base (median of last 3 FY OE/share): −$1.46/share** (latest FY alone: also −$1.46/share — both are −1.455495004541326 in dcf_numbers.json). Both are ≤ 0, so the choice does not change the verdict. No TTM base was used — see STALE_FY below.
- Balance sheet: net debt $57,495M (dcf_numbers.json) — and still rising: the Utility completed $2.2B of bond issuance in June 2026, $4.4B total for H1 2026 (company release, via search results).

## Moat: 5/10 — a real legal monopoly whose prize is capped and whose tail can kill the equity
Justification: legal-monopoly franchise with essential, inelastic demand and unusually visible guided growth (≥9% core EPS growth targeted through 2030, no new equity), plus the scarce Diablo Canyon nuclear asset and 12+ GW of data-center load in the pipeline. But the CPUC caps the economics, the growth is debt-funded, and inverse condemnation leaves a binary wildfire tail that already bankrupted this equity once.
- FOR: legal-monopoly electric/gas franchise across Northern/Central California — essential service, inelastic demand, no customer switching; visible growth — $73B capex plan through 2030, FY2026 core EPS guided $1.64–$1.66, ≥9% core EPS growth targeted through 2030, no new equity required; Diablo Canyon nuclear — scarce carbon-free baseload with renewed license; 12+ GW data-center project pipeline — real load-growth optionality; SB 254 (signed Sep 2025) adds an $18B Wildfire Fund Continuation Account, with PG&E's 2026 disallowance cap ~$5.1B (10-Q summary, via search results).
- AGAINST: inverse condemnation — liable for equipment-caused fires without proof of negligence, the tail that bankrupted the equity in 2019–20; CPUC caps allowed ROE — no pricing power, and the 2027–2030 general rate case is filed into an affordability-first political environment; debt-funded growth — net debt $57,495M at YE2025 and rising, so the equity absorbs any disallowance first; the Continuation Account is authorized, not pre-funded cash — IOU contributions run 2029–2045, PG&E's share is 47.85%, and the original Wildfire Fund is being drawn by Eaton Fire claims; diluted share count creeping up ~1.1%/yr (engine share CAGR), a small per-share drag.
- A 5 gives CAP = 8.5 years — academic here, since there is no positive OE stream to fade.

## DCF — v5 final run (2026-10-14)
The final engine pass was run with moat 5 and default probabilities 10/25/30/25/10 (offsets −12/−5/0/+5/+12pp, multipliers 0.75/0.90/1.00/1.10/1.25), but **the engine emits no scenario table, IV, or IRR: the normalized base OE is −$1.46/share, so there is no positive owner's-earnings path to discount at any scenario weighting.** Tier by numbers: **F**.

| Scenario | Prob | Growth start | OE mult | Story | IV@15 | IRR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Super bear | 10% | n/a | 0.75 | Catastrophic fire year or punitive disallowance | n/a — negative base | n/a |
| Bear | 25% | n/a | 0.90 | Regulatory lag, allowed-ROE cut, capex stays far above OCF | n/a — negative base | n/a |
| Base | 30% | n/a | 1.00 | Capex stays well above OCF indefinitely; conservative OE stays negative | n/a — negative base | n/a |
| Bull | 25% | n/a | 1.10 | Rate-base growth converts to free cash flow sooner than history suggests | n/a — negative base | n/a |
| Super bull | 10% | n/a | 1.25 | Structural FCF inflection plus a durable wildfire-liability fix | n/a — negative base | n/a |

- **Probability-weighted IV/IRR: not computable (negative base). Tier by numbers: F.**
- Sanity check on growth inputs: the engine's blended growth is 4.77% (rev CAGR 5y 6.19%, 3y 4.77%, latest YoY +2.11%; OE/share CAGR not computable on a negative OE series), adjusted −1.08pp for the rising share count. Utility revenue is pass-through-heavy and says little about per-share earning power — the per-share prints (H1 2026 core EPS $0.83 vs $0.64; FY2026 guided $1.64–$1.66; ≥9% targeted through 2030) are healthier than the revenue blend — but growth is irrelevant to the verdict: it multiplies a negative base.
- Recent prints (search results, for the record): the earnings engine is healthy — it is the capex load, not profitability, that zeroes out conservative OE. GAAP net income has risen three straight years (FY2023 $2,256M → FY2024 $2,512M → FY2025 $2,703M, financials_history.csv).

## Flags — every fragility flag resolved
- **STALE_FY** (FY ended 2025-12-31, 9 months ago): ttm.py was run and **exited non-zero (exit 3)**: "ttm.py: cannot compute TTM for PCG (CIK 1004980): sbc: no post-FY YTD fact (no 10-Q since the 2025-12-31 fiscal year end)" — PCG's 10-Q facts do not give ttm.py a usable post-FY YTD SBC leg, so no TTM base exists. Per the sweep rules, the engine's median base (−$1.46/share) is used instead, with the reason stated here. This does not change the outcome: the latest full FY is also negative (−$1.46/share), and the H1 2026 prints (core EPS up, guidance reaffirmed) give no indication capex has fallen below OCF.
- **NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE** (2023, 2024, 2025): resolved — the gap is the standard utility non-cash pattern, not a one-off. Net income vs OCF: 2023 $2,256M vs $4,747M; 2024 $2,512M vs $8,035M; 2025 $2,703M vs $8,716M (financials_history.csv). OCF runs *above* net income persistently — the opposite direction from the tax-deposit pattern this flag was built for — because net income is stated after depreciation on a very large plant base and other non-cash charges that OCF adds back. The engine's D&A exemption cannot clear the flag mechanically because the engine found **no D&A tag at all** for PCG in companyfacts (used_tags da = null) — a tag-coverage gap, not an earnings-quality signal. The conservative OE series is OCF-based throughout, so the divergence does not contaminate the base.
- **SECTOR_MODEL_MISMATCH** (Utilities): accepted in full — the OE/capex DCF fits regulated utilities poorly, because growth capex is rate-base investment earning a regulated return, not value destruction. Confidence is graded **low** and the tier is read as "not modelable on this screen," not as "bad business." The v4 run's workaround (a hand-built core-EPS base) is not available to a v5 worker run: no ttm.py TTM exists, and judgment.json carries no base override for PCG, so the numbers tier stands and no tier override is taken.

## My thoughts / overlay
- **Method range, honestly stated:** the v4 run (2026-10-13) put PCG at Tier B / 18.2% weighted IRR on a hand-built TTM core-EPS base; the v5 run is Tier F on the conservative OE base. The spread is entirely a base-definition artifact for a rate-base grower — neither number should be quoted without its method. What survives both methods: guided core EPS growth of ~9–10% is itself below Andrew's 15% hurdle rate, so even the friendlier earnings definition does not clear 15% on growth alone — it needed a multiple-re-rating argument, which is a regulatory-outcome bet (SB 254 implementation, the 2027–2030 GRC), not an owner's-earnings DCF result.
- The balance sheet belongs in the verdict: net debt $57,495M behind a $29.417B market cap, growing by design under the no-new-equity plan ($4.4B issued in H1 2026 alone). For a regulated utility that leverage is serviced from allowed returns — but it is also why the equity, not the debt, is the shock absorber for any disallowance, restitution, or catastrophic-fire outcome.
- The wildfire backstop improved on paper in 2025–26 (SB 254's $18B Continuation Account; ~$5.1B 2026 disallowance cap; PG&E's contribution share cut to 47.85%) but it is not cash in hand: IOU contributions run 2029–2045, and S&P analysts (via search results) estimate the January 2025 Eaton Fire could draw ~$15B against the original fund for Edison's liabilities alone. One catastrophic PG&E-caused fire remains a solvency event, not a scenario in a table.
- Hurdle-clearing price: not computable from this model — with no positive OE base there is no IV@15% at any price, and stating one would require a different model (earnings-multiple or rate-base), which is out of scope for this sweep. No tier override: the numbers tier F is retained, with the mismatch documented, rather than inventing a tier the v5 method cannot support.

## Final verdict
- **Final tier: F** (tier by numbers F — no positive normalized conservative owner's earnings in any of the last 5 years; OE DCF not supportable)
- Confidence: **Low** (sector-model mismatch: the F is substantially a model artifact for a regulated utility — but no in-method reading clears a 15% hurdle either)
- One-liner: Regulated California monopoly with a binary wildfire tail, moat 5/10, but conservative owner's earnings are negative in all of the last 5 years (capex exceeds OCF every year; normalized base −$1.46/share) — Tier F on this screen; guided ~9–10% core EPS growth does not clear 15% and no hurdle-clearing price is computable on a negative OE base.
